published_prior_art.cite: MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025 supplies separate directed and occupied-rectangle additions, not the stated simultaneous loop-aware profile theorem.
MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025 §3.6 proves only occupied-rectangle bidirected replacement; MogensenHansen2020 uses a different μ-separation walk calculus.
MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025 leaves the all-DMG greatest-element claim as a conjecture after proving only directed and restricted mixed moves.
MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025, §3.6 explicitly conjectures a greatest E-equivalent DMG; its Theorem 3.12 is directed-only.
No published E result found establishes joint mixed saturation; conditional on Theorem 2, this is a natural closure corollary.
MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025 gives directed recovery; the mixed recovery is consequential but follows from the proposed greatest-member theorem plus finite enumeration.
MantenCasoloMogensenKilbertus2025, Theorem 3.12 proves the directed greatest-representative result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Definition 2.1; pp. 9–12, Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.22, and §3.6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published DMG universe uses directed edges V×V and unordered bidirected equivalence classes, hence includes loops; it proves a greatest representative only for DGs, proves the occupied-rectangle mixed bidirected addition, and explicitly conjectures a greatest element for every E-equivalence class of DMGs.
Potential siblings and potential parents yield N(I(G)), which is Markov equivalent under μ-separation and a supergraph of every member of its equivalence class.
The paper establishes soundness and completeness of FCI for simple σ-faithful SCMs with cycles for several graph features, rather than an E-separation greatest-graph theorem.
The proceedings paper presents an efficient procedure for d-separation Markov equivalence of directed graphs that may contain cycles; it is a distinct separation setting from E-separation.
The preprint gives integer-programming graph learning and globally optimal solutions for its formulation, but does not state E-equivalence union closure or an E-greatest-DMG theorem.
The preprint studies separable graphical models and canonical representations for their separation-equivalence classes, not the E-separation DMG conjecture.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a worked two- or three-vertex loop-inclusive DMG that explicitly computes Lift, the mixed SCC profile, Γ, and the first-new-edge replacement certificate; use it to make the bidirected-loop case auditable.

State a short strictness corollary exhibiting a genuinely bidirected E-DMG outside the directed subclass, while formally identifying the directed subclass as the Manten et al. Theorem 3.12 special case.
Separate oracle query complexity from finite enumeration complexity by giving a concrete runtime bound or a constrained-search recovery variant after the structural theorem is established.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with unrestricted contextual lifted-walk replacement as the sole load-bearing solve target; retain saturation and recovery as downstream corollaries.
